title: Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in Epidemic Models
summary: Compartment epidemic models are often linear in coefficients that are physical parameters or products of parameters, so parameter estimation can be reduced to closed-form least squares. The paper introduces physics-informed weak regression (PIWR), which integrates the model in time with cubic-spline quadrature, avoids differentiating noisy data, estimates the initial state jointly, and is wrapped with split conformal prediction using simulated epidemics as the calibration population, plus a residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC). Across eleven DINN benchmarks, PIWR or PIR-FD6 is reported to improve on DINN errors by one to four orders of magnitude where sampling resolves the dynamics, each fit takes about a millisecond, and the 90% simultaneous intervals achieve 87–92% empirical coverage in all 88 tested settings.

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.split: 100 samples on [0,500] days; ε=0.01 noise level
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01
target.config_for_value: PIWR with cubic-spline quadrature and jointly estimated initial state; SIDR parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294; N=59·10^6; 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days; 1 % multiplicative Gaussian noise
target.est_compute: CPU, <1 s including data simulation; single PIWR fit is about 0.2 ms
target.quote: With 1 % noise the error of PIR-FD2 grows to 1.2–1.5 %, while PIR-FD6 and PIWR reach 0.12–0.49 %.

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

requirements.stmt: Formulate the epidemic model in parameter-linear form ẋ = f0(x,t) + A(x,t)θ, with the library A containing no unknown parameters and a map h recovering physical parameters from θ.
requirements.quote: the library A(x, t) ∈Rn×p contains no unknowns

requirements.stmt: For PIWR, use the integrated weak relation x(tj)=x0+Jjθ, with Jj the time integral of the library, instead of differentiating the data.
requirements.quote: The relation is still linear in θ, but it contains the data themselves instead of their derivatives.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate each library entry by a cubic spline with not-a-knot end conditions on the sample grid and integrate the spline exactly to obtain quadrature weights.
requirements.quote: interpolated over t0, . . . , tm−1 by a cubic spline (not-a-knot end conditions), and the spline is integrated exactly from t0 to tj.

requirements.stmt: Estimate the initial state x0 jointly with θ using the augmented system with identity blocks for x0.
requirements.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns, so that the noise of the first sample is not propagated into every equation.

requirements.stmt: Solve the PIWR least-squares problem by a numerically stable orthogonal factorization or SVD-based least squares, not by explicitly forming the normal equations.
requirements.quote: In implementation, we do not form the normal equations (16), whose condition number is the square of that of MD.

requirements.stmt: Column-scale the regression matrix to unit column norm before the solve; scaling is a change of variables and leaves the minimizer unchanged.
requirements.cite: Sections 3.1 and 3.2, equations (11) and implementation after (18)
requirements.quote: the columns are scaled to unit norm before the solve

requirements.stmt: For the synthetic benchmarks, add compartment-wise noise with standard deviation ε times the maximum absolute true compartment value over the time grid.
requirements.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

requirements.stmt: For conformal calibration, draw calibration parameters from a prior box of ±50 % around literature values, capped at 1 for probabilities and [0,c] for parameters whose literature value is zero.
requirements.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

requirements.stmt: Use the maximum normalized error over all parameters as the split-conformal nonconformity score, then form simultaneous intervals with the corresponding quantile.
requirements.quote: To obtain intervals that hold for all k parameters at once, we use the maximum normalized error as the nonconformity score

requirements.stmt: For PIWR-RACC, compute the residual-adaptive factor h = 1 + R/Rbar, with Rbar the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and apply h to scores and intervals.
requirements.quote: with  ̄R the median residual on 200 tuning draws, and use it in the score (20) and the intervals (21).

requirements.stmt: Use 999 calibration problems and α=0.1 for the 90 % simultaneous intervals, with tuning done on separate draws.
requirements.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1.

requirements.stmt: Recover physical parameters through ω=h(θ) and, when uncertainty in ω is reported, propagate the coefficient covariance by the delta method.
requirements.quote: The physical parameters are ˆω = h(ˆθ). Their uncertainty follows from the delta method

requirements.stmt: For the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark, use N=59·10^6, initial state S0=N−1 and I0=1, parameters α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294, and 100 equally spaced samples on [0,500] days.
requirements.cite: Section 2 worked example and Appendix A.1
requirements.quote: 100 equally spaced samples on [0, 500] days (∆t = 5.05 days) of the solution with (α, β, γ) = (0.191, 0.05, 0.0294)

requirements.stmt: Report errors as percent of the actual parameter value, using the median over estimated parameters of a model when summarizing a model.
requirements.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

requirements.stmt: Generate synthetic benchmark trajectories with LSODA at relative and absolute tolerances of 10^-10.
requirements.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The paper does not give the random seed or specify whether the Table 2 PIWR value 0.124 % is from one noise realization, a median over realizations, or a repeated-fit median.
assumptions.chosen: Use a single fixed-seed realization for the point estimate, then check stability over 1,000 realizations at the literature values.
assumptions.quote: for ε = 1 %, on 1,000 noise realizations at the literature values.

assumptions.gap: The paper says row scaling is selected per model on tuning draws but does not state whether the SIDR PIWR run uses Dn=In or compartment-max scaling.
assumptions.chosen: Use Dn=In for SIDR unless a separate tuning run on 100 draws says otherwise.
assumptions.quote: whether to use it (Dn = In otherwise) is decided per model and estimator on a tuning set (section 5.1).

assumptions.gap: The exact definition of the reported single-parameter % error for α is not given beyond the general metric sentence.
assumptions.quote: Errors are reported in percent of the actual value, as the median over the estimated parameters of a model.

assumptions.gap: The initial state x0 is estimated jointly but the paper does not state whether positivity or bounds are imposed on x0.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained least squares, as in the augmented linear system.
assumptions.quote: The initial state x0 is treated as n additional unknowns

assumptions.gap: The exact ODE solver tolerances for the synthetic SIDR data generation are not stated in the main text.
assumptions.quote: integrated with LSODA (Petzold, 1983) at relative and absolute tolerances of 10−10.

assumptions.gap: The printed Δt=5.05 days is rounded; the exact grid construction is not shown.
The population is printed as 59·10^6 in OCR text; the exact integer is not otherwise specified.
The paper does not say whether any smoothing is applied to noisy states before evaluating the library inside the PIWR integrals.
assumptions.chosen: No smoothing; use noisy states directly in the library and integrate by spline.
assumptions.quote: Both PIR and PIWR evaluate the library at the noisy samples.

assumptions.gap: The least-squares rank-deficiency threshold and exact SVD/LAPACK routine are not specified.
assumptions.chosen: numpy.linalg.lstsq with default rcond in float64.

assumptions.gap: The exact joint prior box for α, β, γ in the SIDR calibration is not tabulated parameter by parameter.
assumptions.chosen: Independent uniform [0.5α*,1.5α*], [0.5β*,1.5β*], [0.5γ*,1.5γ*], with no cap binding since all values are below 1.
assumptions.quote: The prior box is ±50 % around the literature values (capped at 1 for probabilities, and [0, c] for the three parameters whose literature value is zero)

assumptions.gap: The random seeds for the 100 row-scaling tuning draws and 200 Rbar tuning draws are not given.
assumptions.chosen: Use separate fixed seeds for row-scaling tuning, Rbar tuning, calibration, and testing.
assumptions.quote: Every estimator is tuned on draws that are not used for calibration or testing: the row scaling on 100 draws,  ̄R on 200 draws.

assumptions.gap: The seed splitting for 999 calibration problems and 2,000 test problems is not specified.
assumptions.chosen: Use fixed seed 0 and disjoint generated pools for calibration and testing.
assumptions.quote: The calibration uses n = 999 problems and α = 0.1. The coverage is measured on 2,000 independent test problems

assumptions.gap: Whether coverage is evaluated for all parameters simultaneously or marginally is not fully explicit in the table rows.
assumptions.chosen: Use simultaneous coverage of all parameters in the model, matching the conformal score.

assumptions.gap: The numerical precision and implementation language for the least-squares solve are not part of the mathematical method but affect exact values.
assumptions.quote: all estimates are dense least-squares solves (numpy.linalg.lstsq) in double precision.

assumptions.gap: Whether the RACC h factor is used for the point estimate or only for interval widths is not explicit in the score formula text.
assumptions.chosen: Apply h only to scores and interval widths; point estimate remains the PIWR least-squares estimate.
assumptions.quote: Scaling the conformal scores and intervals by a factor that increases with this residual widens the intervals for difficult data sets and narrows them for easy ones

assumptions.gap: The paper does not state whether the first and last samples are included in the PIWR linear system beyond saying all samples are used.
assumptions.chosen: Include all m samples, with J0=0 and the measured x0 on the right-hand side.
assumptions.quote: uses all samples, including the end points

assumptions.gap: The paper does not constrain the SIDR parameter estimates to be positive or within a physical range.
assumptions.chosen: Unconstrained linear least squares for the point estimate.
assumptions.quote: PIR and PIWR search an unbounded parameter space

assumptions.gap: The noise scale uses the maximum true compartment value, but the paper does not state whether that maximum is computed before or after adding noise.
assumptions.chosen: Maximum of the true noise-free trajectory per compartment.
assumptions.quote: add noise per compartment c as  ̃xc(ti) = xc(ti)+ε maxt|xc(t)| ξi, ξi ∼N(0, 1)

why: The only linked repository (Shaier/DINN) is the *baseline* the paper benchmarks against, not the paper's own method: it contains 626 files of Jupyter notebooks and CSVs for DINN training, zero Python modules, and no PIWR / PIR-FD / conformal-prediction code at all. The paper's contribution (physics-informed weak regression: integrate the linear-in-parameters SIDR equations in time with cubic-spline quadrature, solve a closed-form least-squares problem with the initial state as a free unknown) exists only as a mathematical description in the text, so it must be reimplemented. The repo is still useful in one narrow way: Diseases/COVID/generate_covid_data.ipynb and sidr.csv pin down the exact SIDR benchmark (N = 59e6, S0 = N-1, I0 = 1, alpha = 0.191, beta = 0.05, gamma = 0.0294, 100 points on [0,500], 1% multiplicative noise), which is the match target for C1, and the data can equally be regenerated from Appendix A.1 alone. The reimplementation is cheap: a 4-state linear ODE system, a cumulative-spline quadrature matrix, and one numpy.linalg.lstsq call.
est_runtime: 5-10 minutes of command time: ~1 min to install numpy/scipy/matplotlib, ~10 s to simulate the SIDR benchmark, milliseconds per PIWR fit, so a few hundred repeated fits plus a noise-level sweep finish in seconds; the remainder is development of the ~200-line weak-form estimator and the clean re-run.
blockers: The linked repository is the DINN baseline (PyTorch 1.8.1, pandas 1.1.5, numpy 1.19.2, Python 3.6) — the paper's own estimator is not in it, so nothing in the repo produces any of the claimed numbers

requirements.txt pins torch/numpy versions that will not install cleanly on this machine's Python 3.12, but that is moot since the DINN baseline is the comparison method and not needed for the match target
No scripts, only notebooks; no CLI entrypoint that emits a target number

The two runs reported for C1 are single noise realizations implicitly (no seed stated), so an exact 0.124% match requires reproducing the same random draw; honest reproduction should report median/mean over realizations and accept a small deviation

approach: Reimplement PIWR for the SIDR benchmark directly from the equations: generate the true trajectory with LSODA at 1e-10 tolerances, and for C1 use the 100-point DINN `sidr.csv` 1% benchmark when available (falling back to a fixed-seed regeneration from Appendix A.1) so the single noise realisation is not invented. For each compartment and each library column, evaluate A(x,t) on the sample grid, interpolate with a not-a-knot cubic spline, integrate the spline exactly to every sample time, and assemble the augmented linear system with x0 as four extra unknowns. Solve the column-normalised system with `numpy.linalg.lstsq` (never forming normal equations), unscale, extract theta=(alpha,beta,gamma), and compute |alpha_hat-0.191|/0.191*100. Add noiseless, stability-over-realizations, and timing checks, then write all numbers to `results/metrics.json`.
steps: Create `config.py` with the exact SIDR parameters, time grid, noise level, LSODA tolerances, spline/quadrature settings, column scaling, lstsq settings, target and tolerance; do not install DINN requirements or run DINN notebooks.
Implement `src/sidr.py`: SIDR RHS with state order [S,I,D,R], LSODA simulation at rtol=atol=1e-10, compartment-wise Gaussian noise per R7, and a flexible CSV loader for the DINN `sidr.csv` benchmark.

Load `Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv` if present; inspect header/columns and confirm there are 100 rows with time plus S,I,D,R. Compare it with a noiseless LSODA trajectory to verify it is the 1% noise file. If it is missing or not the 1% file, use `Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv`; if no candidate CSV exists, regenerate with seed 0.

Implement `src/piwr.py`: for each state c and each library column k, evaluate A_{c,k}(x_noisy(t_i),t_i) on the sample grid, build a not-a-knot CubicSpline, integrate exactly from t_0 to every t_j via the spline antiderivative, and store J[c][j,k].

Build the augmented system M and RHS y: for each state c and time j, set M[row,c]=1 for x0_c and M[row,n_states+k]=J[c][j,k] for theta_k; set y[row]=x_noisy[j,c]. Include all m samples and ensure J[:,0]=0 at j=0.

Column-scale M to unit column norms, solve with `numpy.linalg.lstsq(M_scaled,y,rcond=None)` in float64, unscale coefficients by dividing by the column norms, and extract x0_hat and theta_hat=(alpha_hat,beta_hat,gamma_hat).

Run the noiseless sanity fit on the true trajectory: verify alpha_hat is within about 1e-4% of 0.191 and x0_hat matches the true initial state; if not, debug the SIDR library, spline integration, or state/column mapping before touching the 1% data.
Run the C1 fit on the verified 1% benchmark CSV: compute alpha_hat and `100*abs(alpha_hat-0.191)/0.191`; record whether it lies in [0.1116,0.1364].
Run the stability sweep: regenerate 1000 independent 1% noise realisations with fixed seeds, fit each with PIWR, and store median, mean, IQR and 5–95% range of the alpha percent error.
Run the timing check: repeat the PIWR fit 30 times on the C1 data set and record median CPU milliseconds per fit.

Write `results/metrics.json` with the C1 headline fields (alpha_true, alpha_hat, alpha_rel_error_pct, target_pct, within_tolerance), data source, matrix shape/rank/condition number, x0_hat, beta_hat, gamma_hat, noiseless check, stability summary, timing summary, and the exact config used.

Validate the JSON by re-reading it and printing a summary; verify the headline error is compared against the relative tolerance band and that the noiseless, stability and timing diagnostics are present.
smoke_test: Implement a `--smoke` mode in `reproduce.py` that loads/simulates the SIDR benchmark once, builds M, asserts M.shape==(400,7), asserts J_0==0, checks rank(M_scaled)==7, and runs two fits: (i) noiseless true states, expected alpha error below 1e-4%, and (ii) one noisy 1% realisation, expected alpha error in the 0.05–1% range. This proves the spline quadrature, augmented least squares, scaling, and alpha extraction without the 1000-realisation sweep.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size: t has shape (100,), X_noisy has shape (100,4), all finite; time runs from 0 to 500 inclusive with `np.linspace(0,500,100)`.
True trajectory sanity: S decreases from N-1, I starts at 1 and peaks, D and R are nonnegative and nondecreasing; max absolute value per compartment is nonzero so the R7 noise scale is well defined.

Noise sanity on the benchmark CSV: if using `sidr.csv`, compare it with the noiseless trajectory and verify residuals are approximately N(0, (0.01*max|x_c|)^2); if not, select the correct 100-point 1% noise CSV before fitting.
Matrix sanity: M has shape (4*100,4+3)=(400,7); J at t_0 is exactly zero for every column; after unit-column scaling no column has zero norm; rank is 7 and the scaled condition number is reported.

Noiseless baseline: a PIWR fit to the true states recovers alpha to near machine/quadrature accuracy (target <1e-4% relative error) and gives x0 close to [N-1,1,0,0]; failure here means an equation/library/quadrature bug, not a noise issue.
Single noisy fit sanity: alpha_hat is positive and within a few percent of 0.191; the reported C1 error should be near the paper's 0.124%, not orders of magnitude larger.
Timing sanity: 30 repeated fits on the 100-point SIDR problem should be milliseconds or less on CPU; if a fit takes seconds, the implementation is rebuilding splines or solving the wrong problem.
budget_plan: About 10 minutes of command time: 2 min creating `config.py`, `src/sidr.py`, `src/piwr.py`, `src/evaluate.py`, and `reproduce.py`; 2 min on smoke/noiseless validation and fixing any shape or quadrature bug; 3 min on the C1 fit plus the 1000-realisation stability sweep (each fit is sub-millisecond to millisecond, so the sweep is dominated by data generation and Python overhead); 1 min for the 30-repeat timing check; 2 min for writing, re-reading, and validating `results/metrics.json`.

important discovery! The DINN generator notebook uses:
- dSdt = -(alpha/N)*S*I
- dIdt = (alpha/N)*S*I - beta*I - gamma*I
- **dDdt = gamma*I

**
- **dRdt = beta*I**

So in the DINN convention, D (dead) grows with gamma and R (recovered) grows with beta! This is the opposite of the plan's stated convention ("
dD/dt=beta*I", "dR/dt=gamma*I"). Let me check: the notebook says dDdt = gamma*I and dRdt = beta*I. The plan says "dD/dt=beta*I", "dR/dt=gamma*I". Hmm, so the plan's convention has D

with beta, R with gamma. The DINN notebook has D with gamma, R with beta.

This matters for the naming of parameters but NOT for alpha: the I equation is (alpha/N)*S*I -
beta*I - gamma*I regardless. And the library columns: if we set up the library as dI/dt = alpha*(S*I/N) - beta*I - gamma

*I, then alpha, beta, gamma are all identified the same either way. The D/R equations just swap which column gets which label.

A preprint - October 15, 2026
A physics-based model can generate its own calibration population, which makes split conformal prediction
applicable to model parameters. The resulting simultaneous intervals keep their 90 % coverage in all 88 tested
settings of the DINN benchmarks, and in the S3I3R and real-data cases, are narrow where the estimate is
accurate, and widen where the data do not support the estimate, without access to the true parameters. The
residual-adaptive factor (PIWR-RACC) adapts the width to the difficulty of the individual data set at no
cost in coverage (in the time-varying Case 3 it narrows the bands by a factor of nine). Prior knowledge enters
the same way, where a parameter known only approximately must be drawn from its uncertainty range in
the calibration population, otherwise the intervals lose their coverage, and fixing a parameter narrows the
intervals only of the parameters it decouples.
Acknowledgment
This work was performed at Department of Applied Mathematics and Computer Science, Technical University
of Denmark.
Declaration
The author declare that he had no potential conflicts of interest with respect to the investigation, authorship,
and/or publication of this article.
During the preparation of this work, generative AI tools were used in order to review python code (fx. bug
finding), setup scripts for systematic numerical experiments, and improve language clarity. The author take
full responsibility for the scientific content of the published article. The original ideas of this work was the
outcome of authors human thoughts and creativity.
Code and hardware environment
The code that reproduces every figure and table in section 5 will be available after peer review of the work.
The timings reported in section 5 were measured on a MacBook Pro (Nov 2024, Apple M4 Max, 16 cores, 48
GB RAM). The implementation uses Python with NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. The ODEs are integrated
with LSODA (scipy.integrate.odeint), the weak-form integrals use scipy.interpolate.CubicSpline,
and all estimates are dense least-squares solves (numpy.linalg.lstsq) in double precision. No deep-learning

any computation; the target/tolerance entries are only compared against the
computed value at the very end.

POPULATION_N = 59_000_000.0          # N = 59 * 10^6 (known, R13/A.1)

N_STATES = 4

# omega* = (alpha, beta, gamma)  (A.1, eq. 29)
TRUE_PARAMETERS = {"alpha": 0.191, "beta": 0.05, "gamma": 0.0294}

N_PARAMS = 3

# x0 = (N - 1, 1, 0, 0)  (A.1)
TRUE_X0 = np.array([POPULATION_N - 1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0])

M_SAMPLES = 100                       # 100 equally spaced samples
T_START, T_END = 0.0, 500.0           # on [0, 500] days
TIME_GRID = np.linspace(T_START, T_END, M_SAMPLES)

NOISE_EPSILON = 0.01                  # eps = 1 %  (C1 / R7)

# --------------------------------------------------------------- generation --
# LSODA at rtol = atol = 1e-10 (R15 / Appendix "Data")
SOLVER_METHOD = "LSODA"
SOLVER_RTOL = 1e-10
SOLVER_ATOL = 1e-10

# xi_i ~ N(0,1) independent per compartment and time.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- PIWR ----
SPLINE_BC = "not-a-knot"     # cubic spline with not-a-knot end conditions (R3)

"""SIDR model (Appendix A.1, eq. 28): generation, noise and DINN cross-check.

    dS/dt = -alpha * S * I / N
    dI/dt =  alpha * S * I / N - (beta + gamma) * I
    dD/dt =  gamma * I
    dR/dt =  beta * I

State order (S, I, D, R); population N is known; theta = (alpha, beta, gamma).

The library A(x, t) (n=4 rows, p=3 columns, eq. 5 of the paper) is

              alpha      beta     gamma
    S    [ -S*I/N ,      0    ,      0    ]
    I    [  S*I/N ,     -I    ,     -I    ]
    D    [    0    ,      0    ,      I    ]
    R    [    0    ,      I    ,      0    ]
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

import config as cfg


def rhs(t, y, alpha, beta, gamma, N):
    S, I, D, R = y
    infection = alpha * S * I / N
    return (
        -infection,
        infection - (beta + gamma) * I,
        gamma * I,
        beta * I,
    )


def simulate(t=None, params=None, x0=None, N=None):
    """Integrate the SIDR system with LSODA at rtol = atol = 1e-10 (R15)."""
    t = cfg.TIME_GRID if t is None else np.asarray(t, float)
    params = cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS if params is None else params
    x0 = cfg.TRUE_X0 if x0 is None else np.asarray(x0, float)
    N = cfg.POPULATION_N if N is None else float(N)

    sol = solve_ivp(
        rhs,
        (t[0], t[-1]),
        x0,
        method=cfg.SOLVER_METHOD,
        t_eval=t,
        args=(params["alpha"], params["beta"], params["gamma"], N),
        rtol=cfg.SOLVER_RTOL,
        atol=cfg.SOLVER_ATOL,
    )
    if not sol.success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"LSODA failed: {sol.message}")
    return sol.y.T  # (m, n)


def library(X, t, N=None):
    """Evaluate the library A(x_tilde_i, t_i) at the (possibly noisy) samples.

    Returns an array of shape (m, n, p) so that  xdot ~= A_i @ theta.
    The library is evaluated at the noisy samples themselves (no smoothing),
    exactly as in eq. (12)-(13) of the paper.
    """
    N = cfg.POPULATION_N if N is None else float(N)
    X = np.asarray(X, float)
    m = X.shape[0]
    A = np.zeros((m, cfg.N_STATES, cfg.N_PARAMS))
    S, I, D, R = X[:, 0], X[:, 1], X[:, 2], X[:, 3]
    force = S * I / N
    #                 alpha        beta      gamma
    A[:, 0, 0] = -force            # dS: -alpha * S*I/N
    A[:, 1, 0] = force             # dI: +alpha * S*I/N
    A[:, 1, 1] = -I                #     -beta * I
    A[:, 1, 2] = -I                #     -gamma * I
    A[:, 2, 2] = I                 # dD: +gamma * I
    A[:, 3, 1] = I                 # dR: +beta * I
    return A


def add_noise(X_true, eps, rng):
    """R7 noise: x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi_i."""
    scale = eps * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)     # per compartment
    xi = rng.standard_normal(X_true.shape)
    return X_true + scale * xi, scale


def load_dinn_csv(path):
    """Load a DINN SIDR CSV laid out as rows [t, S, I, D, R]."""
    raw = np.loadtxt(path, delimiter=",")
    if raw.ndim != 2 or raw.shape[0] != 5:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: expected 5 rows [t,S,I,D,R], got {raw.shape}")
    return raw[0], raw[1:].T         # t (m,), X (m, 4)


def check_dinn_reference(t=None, X_true=None, csv_path=None):
    """Cross-check our LSODA trajectory against the DINN published data.

    The paper (Appendix 'Data') states agreement of about 1e-8 relative
    difference with the published files.  The DINN files are noise-free, so
    they validate the generator, not the 1 % benchmark.
    """
    import os

    csv_path = csv_path or cfg.DINN_SIDR_CSV
    if not os.path.exists(csv_path):
        return {"available": False, "path": csv_path}
    t_csv, X_csv = load_dinn_csv(csv_path)
    t = cfg.TIME_GRID if t is None else t
    X_true = simulate(t) if X_true is None else X_true
    ok_grid = (
        t_csv.shape == t.shape
        and np.allclose(t_csv, t, rtol=0, atol=1e-9)
    )
    if ok_grid:
        rel = np.max(np.abs(X_csv - X_true) / np.maximum(np.abs(X_true), 1e-30))
    else:
        rel = float("nan")
    return {
        "available": True,
        "path": csv_path,
        "shape": list(X_csv.shape),
        "grid_matches": bool(ok_grid),
        "max_rel_diff_vs_lsoda": float(rel),
        "is_noise_free": bool(ok_grid and rel < 1e-6),
    }

"""PIWR: physics-informed weak regression (paper sections 3.2, 3.3).

    x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta ,   J_j = int_{t0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds        (12)
    J_j  ~= sum_i w_ji A_i   with cubic-spline (not-a-knot) quadrature    (13)
    M z = y ,  z = (theta, x0) ,  M = diag blocks [J_j | I_n]             (14)

The spline is linear in its data, so the quadrature is a fixed weight matrix
W (m x m) that depends only on the time grid:  J = W @ A_i  for every library
column.  W is built once per grid by integrating the not-a-knot cubic spline
antiderivative of each unit basis vector.
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

import config as cfg


def quadrature_weights(t):
    """Weights w_ji of eq. (13): exact integral of the not-a-knot cubic
    spline through unit vectors e_i, from t_0 to t_j.  W[0, :] == 0 so J_0 = 0.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    m = t.size
    W = np.zeros((m, m))
    for i in range(m):
        d = np.zeros(m)
        d[i] = 1.0
        anti = CubicSpline(t, d, bc_type=cfg.SPLINE_BC).antiderivative()
        W[:, i] = anti(t) - anti(t[0])
    return W


def integrate_library(A, W):
    """J_j = sum_i w_ji A_i for every (state, coefficient) entry. (m, n, p)."""
    return np.einsum("ji,icp->jcp", W, A)


def _assemble(J, X_tilde, row_scaling):
    """Stack eq. (14): M = [[J_0, I_n], ..., [J_{m-1}, I_n]], y = x~."""
    m, n, p = J.shape
    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    I_n = np.eye(n)
    for j in range(m):
        blk = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
        M[blk, :p] = J[j]
        M[blk, p:] = I_n
        y[blk] = X_tilde[j]
    if row_scaling == "none":
        D = np.eye(n)
    elif row_scaling == "compartment-max":
        s = np.max(np.abs(X_tilde), axis=0)          # s_c = max_i |x~_i,c|
        if np.any(s <= 0):
            raise ValueError("degenerate compartment magnitude for row scaling")
        D = np.diag(1.0 / s)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown row scaling {row_scaling!r}")
    # D = I_m kron D_n applied blockwise
    M = (D @ M[blk, :].T).T if False else None  # placeholder, replaced below
    return M, y, D, n, p, m


def build_system(J, X_tilde, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING):
    """Assemble (optionally row-scaled) M, y of eq. (14)-(15)."""
    m, n, p = J.shape
    I_n = np.eye(n)
    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    for j in range(m):
        blk = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
        M[blk, :p] = J[j]
        M[blk, p:] = I_n
        y[blk] = X_tilde[j]
    if row_scaling == "compartment-max":
        s = np.max(np.abs(X_tilde), axis=0)
        if np.any(s <= 0):
            raise ValueError("degenerate compartment magnitude for row scaling")
        Dn = np.diag(1.0 / s)
        for j in range(m):
            blk = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
            M[blk, :] = (Dn @ M[blk, :].T).T
            y[blk] = Dn @ X_tilde[j]
    elif row_scaling != "none":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown row scaling {row_scaling!r}")
    return M, y


def solve_lstsq(M, y):
    """Column-normalised SVD least squares (R5, R6); never normal equations."""
    norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    if np.any(norms == 0):
        raise ValueError("zero column norm: unidentifiable column")
    C = 1.0 / norms
    z, _, rank, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(M * C, y, rcond=None)
    return z / C, rank, norms, C


def fit_piwr(X_tilde, t, W, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING, full=False):
    """One PIWR fit (about a millisecond).  Returns theta, x0 and diagnostics.

    X_tilde : (m, n) measured (possibly noisy) states
    t       : (m,) sample times
    W       : (m, m) precomputed quadrature weights (quadrature_weights(t))
    """
    X_tilde = np.asarray(X_tilde, float)
    A = np.stack([  # library evaluated at the samples (no smoothing)
        X_tilde[:, 0] * X_tilde[:, 1],
        X_tilde[:, 1],
        X_tilde[:, 1],
    ], axis=1)  # placeholder, replaced below
    return A


def piwr(X_tilde, t, W=None, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING, return_aux=False):
    """Full PIWR estimator for the SIDR model.

    Returns a dict with alpha, beta, gamma, x0, standard errors and the
    relative residual R of eq. (23).
    """
    X_tilde = np.asarray(X_tilde, float)

    m, n = X_tilde.shape

        W = quadrature_weights(t)

    N = cfg.POPULATION_N
    force = X_tilde[:, 0] * X_tilde[:, 1] / N          # S*I/N at the samples
    # library columns: c0 = force (alpha), c1 = -I, c2 = -I  with sign fixes
    # per row: S:[-force,0,0] I:[force,-I,-I] D:[0,0,I] R:[0,I,0]

    cols[:, 1, 0] = force

    x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta ,   J_j = int_{t0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds        (12)
    J_j  ~= sum_i w_ji A_i   with cubic-spline (not-a-knot) quadrature    (13)
    M z = y ,  z = (theta, x0) ,  M = [[J_j, I_n]] blocks                 (14)

The spline is linear in its data, so the quadrature is a fixed weight matrix
W (m x m) that depends only on the time grid:  J_j = sum_i w_ji A_i for every
library entry.  W is built once per grid by integrating the not-a-knot cubic
spline antiderivative of each unit basis vector (R3).
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

import config as cfg


def quadrature_weights(t):
    """Weights w_ji of eq. (13): exact integral of the not-a-knot cubic spline
    through unit vectors e_i, from t_0 to t_j.  W[0, :] == 0 so that J_0 = 0.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    m = t.size
    W = np.zeros((m, m))
    for i in range(m):
        d = np.zeros(m)
        d[i] = 1.0
        anti = CubicSpline(t, d, bc_type=cfg.SPLINE_BC).antiderivative()
        W[:, i] = anti(t) - anti(t[0])
    return W


def integrate_library(A, W):
    """J_j = sum_i w_ji A_i for every (state, coefficient) entry. (m, n, p)."""
    return np.einsum("ji,icp->jcp", W, A)


def sidr_library(X_tilde):
    """A(x~, t) at the samples themselves (no smoothing), shape (m, n, p).

              alpha      beta     gamma
    S    [ -S*I/N ,      0    ,      0    ]
    I    [  S*I/N ,     -I    ,     -I    ]
    D    [    0    ,      0    ,      I    ]
    R    [    0    ,      I    ,      0    ]
    (paper eq. 5)
    """
    m = X_tilde.shape[0]
    n, p = cfg.N_STATES, cfg.N_PARAMS
    A = np.zeros((m, n, p))
    force = X_tilde[:, 0] * X_tilde[:, 1] / cfg.POPULATION_N   # S*I/N
    I = X_tilde[:, 1]
    A[:, 0, 0] = -force          # dS = -alpha S I/N
    A[:, 1, 0] = force           # dI = +alpha S I/N - (beta+gamma) I
    A[:, 1, 1] = -I
    A[:, 1, 2] = -I
    A[:, 2, 2] = I               # dD = +gamma I
    A[:, 3, 1] = I               # dR = +beta I
    return A


def build_system(J, X_tilde, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING):
    """Assemble the (optionally row-scaled) M, y of eq. (14)-(15)."""
    m, n, p = J.shape
    I_n = np.eye(n)
    M = np.zeros((m * n, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(m * n)
    for j in range(m):
        blk = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
        M[blk, :p] = J[j]
        M[blk, p:] = I_n
        y[blk] = X_tilde[j]
    if row_scaling == "compartment-max":
        s = np.max(np.abs(X_tilde), axis=0)
        if np.any(s <= 0):
            raise ValueError("degenerate compartment magnitude for row scaling")
        Dn = np.diag(1.0 / s)
        for j in range(m):
            blk = slice(j * n, (j + 1) * n)
            M[blk, :] = (Dn @ M[blk, :].T).T
            y[blk] = Dn @ X_tilde[j]
    elif row_scaling != "none":
        raise ValueError(f"unknown row scaling {row_scaling!r}")
    return M, y


def solve_lstsq(M, y):
    """Column-normalised SVD least squares (R5, R6); never normal equations."""
    norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    if np.any(norms == 0):
        raise ValueError("zero column norm: unidentifiable column")
    C = 1.0 / norms
    z, _, rank, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(M * C, y, rcond=None)
    return z / C, int(rank), norms, C


def piwr(X_tilde, t, W=None, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING, covariance=False):
    """One PIWR fit (sub-millisecond with precomputed weights).

    Returns a dict with alpha, beta, gamma, x0, the relative residual R of
    eq. (23) and, if covariance=True, the eq. (18) standard errors.
    """
    X_tilde = np.asarray(X_tilde, float)
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    m, n = X_tilde.shape
    p = cfg.N_PARAMS
    if W is None:
        W = quadrature_weights(t)

    J = integrate_library(sidr_library(X_tilde), W)    # (m, n, p)
    M, y = build_system(J, X_tilde, row_scaling=row_scaling)
    z, rank, norms, C = solve_lstsq(M, y)

    theta, x0 = z[:p], z[p:]
    resid = y - M @ z
    R_rel = float(np.linalg.norm(resid) / np.linalg.norm(y))   # eq. (23)

    out = {
        "alpha": float(theta[0]),
        "beta": float(theta[1]),
        "gamma": float(theta[2]),
        "x0": [float(v) for v in x0],
        "residual_rel": R_rel,
        "aux": {
            "matrix_shape": [int(M.shape[0]), int(M.shape[1])],
            "rank": rank,
            "condition_number_scaled": float(
                np.linalg.cond(M * C)
            ),
        },
    }
    if covariance:
        Ms = M * C
        H = np.linalg.pinv(Ms.T @ Ms)                  # (Ms^T Ms)^{-1}
        sigma2 = float(resid @ resid / (m * n - p - n))          # eq. (18)
        Hfull = H / np.outer(C, C)                     # unscale
        se = np.sqrt(np.maximum(np.diag(sigma2 * Hfull[:p, :p]), 0.0))
        out["aux"]["sigma_bar_sq"] = sigma2
        out["aux"]["std_err"] = {k: float(v) for k, v in zip(cfg.PARAM_ORDER, se)}
    return out

"""Evaluation helpers: percent errors, stability sweep, timing (R14, C2, C5)."""

import time

import numpy as np

import config as cfg
from src import piwr as P
from src import sidr as S


def pct_error(estimate, actual):
    """Percent of the actual value (R14)."""
    return 100.0 * abs(estimate - actual) / abs(actual)


def alpha_pct_error(fit):
    return pct_error(fit["alpha"], cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS["alpha"])


def model_pct_errors(fit):
    return {
        name: pct_error(fit[name], cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS[name])
        for name in cfg.PARAM_ORDER
    }


def summarize(errors):
    e = np.asarray(errors, float)
    q25, q75 = np.percentile(e, [25, 75])
    return {
        "n": int(e.size),
        "median": float(np.median(e)),
        "mean": float(e.mean()),
        "std": float(e.std(ddof=1)) if e.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "iqr": [float(q25), float(q75)],
        "p05_p95": [float(np.percentile(e, 5)), float(np.percentile(e, 95))],
        "min": float(e.min()),
        "max": float(e.max()),
    }


def stability_sweep(X_true, t, W, n_realizations, eps, seed_base):
    """Independent 1 % noise realizations at the literature values.

    Returns per-seed alpha errors and a summary.  Deterministic given the seed
    base (numpy.random.default_rng(seed_base + i) for realization i).
    """
    errs = np.empty(n_realizations)
    alpha_hats = np.empty(n_realizations)
    for i in range(n_realizations):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_base + i)
        X_noisy, _ = S.add_noise(X_true, eps, rng)
        fit = P.piwr(X_noisy, t, W)
        errs[i] = alpha_pct_error(fit)
        alpha_hats[i] = fit["alpha"]
    return errs, alpha_hats


def median_seed(errs, seed_base):
    """Seed whose realization realizes the median alpha error."""
    order = np.argsort(errs, kind="stable")
    return int(seed_base + order[len(order) // 2])


def timing(X_data, t, W, repeats):
    """Median CPU milliseconds per fit over `repeats` repeats of one data set."""
    times = np.empty(repeats)
    for i in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        P.piwr(X_data, t, W)
        times[i] = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3
    return {
        "repeats": int(repeats),
        "median_ms": float(np.median(times)),
        "mean_ms": float(times.mean()),
        "min_ms": float(times.min()),
        "max_ms": float(times.max()),
        "per_call_ms": [float(v) for v in times],
    }

"""Reproduce claim C1 (and the C2/C5 diagnostics) of the paper:
"Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in
Epidemic Models" (arXiv:2610.19058).

C1: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate alpha with 0.124 %
    relative error at 1 % measurement noise (100 samples on [0, 500] days).
C2: noise-free PIWR alpha relative error (reported 0.000105 %).
C5: median CPU time of a PIWR fit (reported 0.21 ms).

    python reproduce.py            # full run, writes results/metrics.json

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

import config as cfg
from src import evaluate as E
from src import piwr as P
from src import sidr as S

RESULTS_DIR = "results"


def build_benchmark():
    """LSODA trajectory on the paper's grid + quadrature weights."""
    t = cfg.TIME_GRID
    X_true = S.simulate(t)
    W = P.quadrature_weights(t)
    return t, X_true, W


def check_data(t, X_true):
    """Intermediate checks on the generated benchmark (plan, data sanity)."""
    checks = {}
    checks["t_shape"] = list(t.shape)
    checks["t_endpoints"] = [float(t[0]), float(t[-1])]
    checks["t_linspace_ok"] = bool(
        t.shape == (cfg.M_SAMPLES,)
        and np.isclose(t[0], cfg.T_START)
        and np.isclose(t[-1], cfg.T_END)
        and np.allclose(np.diff(t), (cfg.T_END - cfg.T_START) / (cfg.M_SAMPLES - 1))
    )
    checks["X_shape"] = list(X_true.shape)
    checks["X_finite"] = bool(np.all(np.isfinite(X_true)))
    S_c, I_c, D_c, R_c = (X_true[:, k] for k in range(4))
    checks["S0_is_N_minus_1"] = bool(np.isclose(S_c[0], cfg.POPULATION_N - 1))
    checks["S_monotone_down"] = bool(np.all(np.diff(S_c) <= 1e-9))
    checks["I0_is_1"] = bool(np.isclose(I_c[0], 1.0))
    checks["I_has_peak"] = bool(np.argmax(I_c) not in (0, cfg.M_SAMPLES - 1))
    checks["D_R_nonneg_nondecreasing"] = bool(
        np.all(D_c >= -1e-6) and np.all(R_c >= -1e-6)
        and np.all(np.diff(D_c) >= -1e-6) and np.all(np.diff(R_c) >= -1e-6)
    )
    checks["compartment_max"] = {
        name: float(np.max(np.abs(X_true[:, k])))
        for k, name in enumerate(cfg.STATE_ORDER)
    }
    checks["ok"] = all(
        v for k, v in checks.items() if isinstance(v, bool)
    )
    return checks


def noiseless_check(t, X_true, W):
    """C2: fit the noise-free trajectory; quadrature error only."""
    fit = P.piwr(X_true, t, W, covariance=True)
    errs = E.model_pct_errors(fit)
    return {
        "alpha_pct_error": errs["alpha"],
        "beta_pct_error": errs["beta"],
        "gamma_pct_error": errs["gamma"],
        "alpha_hat": fit["alpha"],
        "beta_hat": fit["beta"],
        "gamma_hat": fit["gamma"],
        "x0_hat": fit["x0"],
        "x0_abs_error": [
            float(abs(a - b)) for a, b in zip(fit["x0"], cfg.TRUE_X0)
        ],
        "std_err": fit["aux"]["std_err"],
        "residual_rel": fit["residual_rel"],
    }


def matrix_check(X_noisy, t, W):
    """Shape/rank/quadrature sanity of the augmented system (plan)."""
    J = P.integrate_library(P.sidr_library(X_noisy), W)
    M, y = P.build_system(J, X_noisy)
    _, rank, norms, C = P.solve_lstsq(M, y)
    cond = float(np.linalg.cond(M * C))
    return {
        "M_shape": list(M.shape),
        "expected_shape": [cfg.M_SAMPLES * cfg.N_STATES,

        "J0_is_zero": bool(np.max(np.abs(J[0])) == 0.0),
        "rank": int(rank),
        "full_rank": bool(rank == cfg.N_PARAMS + cfg.N_STATES),
        "scaled_condition_number": cond,
    }

def deriv(y, t, alpha, betta, gamma):
    S, I, D, R = y
    dSdt = - (alpha / N) * S * I
    dIdt = (alpha / N) * S * I - beta * I - gamma * I 
    dDdt = gamma * I
    dRdt = beta * I

    return dSdt, dIdt, dDdt, dRdt

def add_noise(X_true, epsilon, rng, variant="independent"):
    """Compartment-wise noise of R7:  x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max|x_c| * xi.

    variant:
      "independent" - xi drawn independently per compartment and time index
                      (the reading used for the headline value).
      "shared-time" - literal R7 subscripting: ONE xi_i per time index, shared
                      by all four compartments (fully correlated across states).
    """
    X_true = np.asarray(X_true, float)
    scale = epsilon * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
    if variant == "independent":
        xi = rng.normal(size=X_true.shape)
    elif variant == "shared-time":
        xi = rng.normal(size=X_true.shape[0])[:, None]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown noise variant: {variant}")
    X_noisy = X_true + scale[None, :] * xi
    return X_noisy, scale

"""PIWR: physics-informed weak regression (paper sections 3.2, 3.3).

    x(t_j) = x0 + J_j theta ,   J_j = int_{t0}^{t_j} A(x(s), s) ds        (12)
    J_j  ~= sum_i w_ji A_i   with cubic-spline (not-a-knot) quadrature    (13)
    M z = y ,  z = (theta, x0) ,  M = [[J_j, I_n]] blocks                 (14)

The spline is linear in its data, so the quadrature is a fixed weight matrix
W (m x m) that depends only on the time grid:  J_j = sum_i w_ji A_i for every
library entry.  W is built once per grid by integrating the not-a-knot cubic
spline antiderivative of each unit basis vector (R3).

fit_with() is the single reusable fitting core: it takes the integral library
J indexed [j][c][k], optionally restricted to a subset of state row blocks
(row-block diagnostics) and/or a library that is not the one of the noisy
samples (clean-library and smoothed-library controls).  piwr() is the
paper-faithful wrapper (library evaluated at the noisy samples, no smoothing,
as stated on p. 17 and in section 5.10 of the paper).
"""

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

import config as cfg


def quadrature_weights(t):
    """Weights w_ji of eq. (13): exact integral of the not-a-knot cubic spline
    through unit vectors e_i, from t_0 to t_j.  W[0, :] == 0 so that J_0 = 0.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    m = t.size
    W = np.zeros((m, m))
    for i in range(m):
        d = np.zeros(m)
        d[i] = 1.0
        anti = CubicSpline(t, d, bc_type=cfg.SPLINE_BC).antiderivative()
        W[:, i] = anti(t) - anti(t[0])
    return W


def integrate_library(A, W):
    """J_j = sum_i w_ji A_i for every (state, coefficient) entry. (m, n, p)."""
    return np.einsum("ji,icp->jcp", W, A)


def sidr_library(X_tilde):
    """A(x~, t) at the samples themselves (no smoothing), shape (m, n, p).

              alpha      beta     gamma
    S    [ -S*I/N ,      0    ,      0    ]
    I    [  S*I/N ,     -I    ,     -I    ]
    D    [    0    ,      0    ,      I    ]
    R    [    0    ,      I    ,      0    ]
    (paper eq. 5)
    """
    m = X_tilde.shape[0]
    n, p = cfg.N_STATES, cfg.N_PARAMS
    A = np.zeros((m, n, p))
    force = X_tilde[:, 0] * X_tilde[:, 1] / cfg.POPULATION_N   # S*I/N
    I = X_tilde[:, 1]
    A[:, 0, 0] = -force          # dS = -alpha S I/N
    A[:, 1, 0] = force           # dI = +alpha S I/N - (beta+gamma) I
    A[:, 1, 1] = -I
    A[:, 1, 2] = -I
    A[:, 2, 2] = I               # dD = +gamma I
    A[:, 3, 1] = I               # dR = +beta I
    return A


def _assemble(J, X_tilde, states):
    """Rows of eq. (14) for the selected state blocks.  J indexed [j][c][k]."""
    m, n = X_tilde.shape
    p = cfg.N_PARAMS
    states = tuple(range(n)) if states is None else tuple(states)
    M = np.zeros((len(states) * m, p + n))
    y = np.zeros(len(states) * m)
    r = 0
    for c in states:
        for j in range(m):
            M[r, :p] = J[j][c]
            M[r, p + c] = 1.0
            y[r] = X_tilde[j, c]
            r += 1
    return M, y, states


def _row_scale(M, y, X_tilde, states, m, row_scaling):
    """D_n = diag(1/max_t|x_c|) applied to each state's row block, or none."""
    if row_scaling == "none":
        return M, y
    if row_scaling == "compartment-max":
        s = np.max(np.abs(X_tilde), axis=0)
        if np.any(s <= 0):
            raise ValueError("degenerate compartment magnitude for row scaling")
        s_inv = 1.0 / s                                     # length n
        for i, c in enumerate(states):
            blk = slice(i * m, (i + 1) * m)
            M[blk] *= s_inv[c]
            y[blk] *= s_inv[c]
        return M, y
    raise ValueError(f"unknown row scaling {row_scaling!r}")


def fit_with(X_tilde, J, states=None, row_scaling=cfg.ROW_SCALING,
             covariance=False):
    """Reusable PIWR core: solve eq. (14) for a given integral library.

    X_tilde : (m, n) noisy samples (the left-hand side of the weak form).
    J       : (m, n, p) integrated library, indexed J[j][c][k] = int A_ck ds.
    states  : optional subset of state row blocks to fit (diagnostics).  theta
              columns that are identically zero on the selected rows (e.g.
              beta/gamma on the S rows alone) are excluded from the scaled
              solve instead of raising; their estimate is NaN and the column
              itself is never modified.
    Returns the same dict as piwr().
    """
    X_tilde = np.asarray(X_tilde, float)
    m, n = X_tilde.shape
    p = cfg.N_PARAMS
    M, y, states = _assemble(J, X_tilde, states)
    M, y = _row_scale(M, y, X_tilde, states, m, row_scaling)

    norms = np.linalg.norm(M, axis=0)
    live = norms > 0
    z = np.full(p + n, np.nan)
    C = np.zeros(p + n)
    cond = float("nan")
    if live.any():
        Clive = 1.0 / norms[live]
        Ms = M[:, live] * Clive                       # unit column norms (R6)
        z_s, _, rank, _ = np.linalg.lstsq(Ms, y, rcond=None)   # SVD lsq (R5)
        z[live] = z_s * Clive                         # unscale: z = C z_s
        C[live] = Clive
        if rank == int(live.sum()):
            cond = float(np.linalg.cond(Ms))
    theta, x0 = z[:p], z[p:]

    resid = y - M @ np.where(np.isnan(z), 0.0, z)
    R_rel = float(np.linalg.norm(resid) / np.linalg.norm(y))   # eq. (23)

    out = {
        "alpha": float(theta[0]) if not np.isnan(theta[0]) else float("nan"),
        "beta": float(theta[1]) if not np.isnan(theta[1]) else float("nan"),
        "gamma": float(theta[2]) if not np.isnan(theta[2]) else float("nan"),
        "x0": [float(v) for v in x0],
        "residual_rel": R_rel,
        "aux": {
            "states": list(states),
            "live_columns": [int(v) for v in np.flatnonzero(live)],
            "rank": int(np.sum(live)) if live.any() else 0,
            "condition_number_scaled": cond,
        },
    }
    if covariance and live.any():
        Ms = M[:, live] * C[live]
        H = np.linalg.pinv(Ms.T @ Ms)                  # (Ms^T Ms)^{-1}

"""Evaluation helpers: percent errors, sweeps and diagnostics (R14, C2, C5).

All numbers reported in results/metrics.json are produced by the functions in
this module; nothing is hard-coded.
"""

import time

import numpy as np
from scipy.interpolate import CubicSpline

import config as cfg
from src import piwr as P
from src import sidr as S


def pct_error(estimate, actual):
    """Percent of the actual value (R14)."""
    return 100.0 * abs(estimate - actual) / abs(actual)


def alpha_pct_error(fit):
    return pct_error(fit["alpha"], cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS["alpha"])


def model_pct_errors(fit):
    return {
        name: pct_error(fit[name], cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS[name])
        for name in cfg.PARAM_ORDER
    }


def summarize(errors):
    e = np.asarray(errors, float)
    q25, q75 = np.percentile(e, [25, 75])
    return {
        "n": int(e.size),
        "median": float(np.median(e)),
        "mean": float(e.mean()),
        "std": float(e.std(ddof=1)) if e.size > 1 else 0.0,
        "iqr": [float(q25), float(q75)],
        "p05_p95": [float(np.percentile(e, 5)), float(np.percentile(e, 95))],
        "min": float(e.min()),
        "max": float(e.max()),
    }


def stability_sweep(X_true, t, W, n_realizations, eps, seed_base,
                    variant="independent", row_scaling="none",
                    library="noisy"):
    """Independent noise realizations at the literature values (A1/A20).

    variant: "independent" (per compartment and time) or "shared-time" (one
    xi per time index, shared by all compartments - the literal R7 reading).
    library: "noisy" (paper), "clean" (noise-free states) or "smooth"
    (spline-smoothed states) - the regressor-noise diagnostic.
    Returns (errors, alpha_hats); deterministic given seed_base.
    """
    errs = np.empty(n_realizations)
    alpha_hats = np.empty(n_realizations)
    for i in range(n_realizations):
        rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_base + i)
        X_noisy, _ = S.add_noise(X_true, eps, rng, variant=variant)
        fit = P.piwr(X_noisy, t, W, row_scaling=row_scaling, library=library)
        errs[i] = alpha_pct_error(fit)
        alpha_hats[i] = fit["alpha"]
    return errs, alpha_hats


def median_seed(errs, seed_base):
    """Seed whose realization realizes the median alpha error."""
    order = np.argsort(errs, kind="stable")
    return int(seed_base + order[len(order) // 2])


def timing(X_data, t, W, repeats):
    """Median CPU milliseconds per fit over `repeats` repeats of one data set."""
    times = np.empty(repeats)
    for i in range(repeats):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        P.piwr(X_data, t, W)
        times[i] = (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1e3
    return {
        "repeats": int(repeats),
        "median_ms": float(np.median(times)),
        "mean_ms": float(times.mean()),
        "min_ms": float(times.min()),
        "max_ms": float(times.max()),
    }


# ----------------------------------------------------- R3 verification -------

def quadrature_exactness(t):
    """R3 implementation check: the weights W must integrate the not-a-knot
    cubic spline exactly, i.e. W @ f == antiderivative(f-spline)(t) - ant(t0)
    for smooth f.  Verified on two smooth test functions.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    W = P.quadrature_weights(t)
    worst = 0.0
    scale = 0.0
    for f, F in ((np.sin, lambda s: -np.cos(s) + np.cos(s[0])),
                 (np.exp, np.exp)):
        vals = f(t)
        exact = F(t) if callable(F) else F(t)
        err = float(np.max(np.abs(W @ vals - exact)))
        worst = max(worst, err)
        scale = max(scale, float(np.max(np.abs(exact))))
    return {"max_abs_error": worst, "relative": worst / scale,
            "exact_to_machine": bool(worst / scale < 1e-12)}


def balance_error(X_true, t, W):
    """R3 method check on the noise-free trajectory: x(t_j) - x(t_0) must equal
    J_j theta* (the spline-integrated library with the true parameters).
    The residual is the spline interpolation error of the sampled library at
    spacing dt - a property of grid + dynamics, not a weight bug (see
    quadrature_convergence).
    """
    X = np.asarray(X_true, float)
    theta = np.array([cfg.TRUE_PARAMETERS[k] for k in cfg.PARAM_ORDER])
    J = P.integrate_library(P.sidr_library(X), W)
    drop = X - X[0]                       # (m, n)
    model = J @ theta                     # (m, n) = sum_k theta_k J[j,c,k]
    err = np.max(np.abs(drop - model), axis=0)
    scale = np.max(np.abs(drop), axis=0)
    rel = err / np.maximum(scale, 1e-300)
    return {
        "abs_per_compartment": [float(v) for v in err],
        "rel_per_compartment": [float(v) for v in rel],
        "rel_max": float(np.max(rel)),
    }


def quadrature_convergence(t_base):
    """4th-order check: the balance error must fall ~16x per grid doubling if
    the quadrature weights are the exact spline integrals (R3)."""
    out = {}
    for m in (100, 200, 400):

    out["ratio_100_to_200"] = out["m100"] / out["m200"]
    out["ratio_200_to_400"] = out["m200"] / out["m400"]
    out["fourth_order"] = bool(

"""Reproduce claim C1 (with C2/C5 diagnostics) of the paper:

"Conformalized Physics-Informed Weak Regression for Parameter Estimation in
Epidemic Models" (arXiv:2610.19058).

C1: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate alpha from 100 samples
    on [0, 500] days at 1 % measurement noise (paper reports 0.124 % error for
    one unstated noise realization).
C2: noise-free PIWR alpha error diagnostic.
C5: median CPU time of a PIWR fit (30 repeats).

The locked configuration is the one the paper's text supports (p. 17 and
section 5.10): the library is evaluated at the noisy samples, no smoothing;
row scaling selected by the paper's own tuning protocol (section 5.9); noise
per compartment and time index (R7).

Usage:
    python reproduce.py            # full run, writes results/metrics.json
    python reproduce.py --smoke    # fast self-checks, no metrics.json
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import time

import numpy as np

import config as cfg
from src import evaluate as E
from src import piwr as P
from src import sidr as S

RESULTS_DIR = "results"
METRICS_PATH = os.path.join(RESULTS_DIR, "metrics.json")

DINN_CSVS = {
    "Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv": "repo/Diseases/COVID/sidr.csv",
    "COVID_Tutorial.csv": "repo/COVID_Tutorial.csv",
}


def contract_band():
    """Tolerance band around the paper's reported value (claim contract C1)."""
    t = cfg.PAPER_TARGET_PCT
    return t * (1.0 - cfg.TOLERANCE_REL), t * (1.0 + cfg.TOLERANCE_REL)


def build_benchmark():
    """LSODA trajectory on the paper's grid + spline-quadrature weights."""
    t = cfg.TIME_GRID
    X_true = S.simulate(t)
    W = P.quadrature_weights(t)
    return t, X_true, W


def check_data(t, X_true):
    """Intermediate data checks (plan) + cross-check against the DINN CSVs."""
    finite = bool(np.all(np.isfinite(X_true)))
    S_col, I_col, D_col, R_col = (X_true[:, k] for k in range(4))
    checks = {
        "t_shape": [int(t.size)],
        "t_range": [float(t[0]), float(t[-1])],
        "t_uniform": bool(np.allclose(np.diff(t), np.diff(t)[0])),
        "X_shape": [int(v) for v in X_true.shape],
        "finite": finite,
        "S_starts_at_N_minus_1": bool(abs(S_col[0] - (cfg.POPULATION_N - 1)) < 1e-6),
        "S_nonincreasing": bool(np.all(np.diff(S_col) <= 1e-6)),
        "I_starts_at_1": bool(abs(I_col[0] - 1.0) < 1e-12),
        "I_has_interior_peak": bool(int(np.argmax(I_col)) not in (0, int(I_col.size) - 1)),
        "D_R_nonnegative_nondecreasing": bool(
            np.all(D_col >= -1e-9) and np.all(np.diff(D_col) >= -1e-9)
            and np.all(R_col >= -1e-9) and np.all(np.diff(R_col) >= -1e-9)),
        "compartment_max": {c: float(v) for c, v in zip(cfg.STATE_ORDER,
                                                        np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0))},
    }
    dinn = {}
    for name, path in DINN_CSVS.items():
        if os.path.exists(path):
            d = np.loadtxt(path, delimiter=",")     # rows: t, S, I, D, R
            Xc = d[1:5, :].T
            dinn[name] = float(np.max(np.abs(Xc - X_true)) / np.max(np.abs(X_true)))
    checks["dinn_trajectory_cross_check_max_rel_diff"] = dinn
    return checks


def r3_checks(t, X_true, W):
    """Verify the quadrature (R3): weights exact, noiseless balances, 4th order."""
    return {
        "weights_exact_vs_antiderivative": E.quadrature_exactness(t),
        "noise_free_balance": E.balance_error(X_true, t, W),
        "grid_convergence": E.quadrature_convergence(t),
    }


def noiseless_check(X_true, t, W):
    """C2 diagnostic: PIWR on the noise-free trajectory."""
    fit = P.piwr(X_true, t, W, covariance=True)
    x0 = np.asarray(fit["x0"])
    return {
        "alpha_hat": fit["alpha"],
        "beta_hat": fit["beta"],
        "gamma_hat": fit["gamma"],
        "pct_errors": E.model_pct_errors(fit),
        "x0_hat": [float(v) for v in x0],
        "x0_max_rel_err": float(np.max(np.abs(x0 - cfg.TRUE_X0)) / cfg.POPULATION_N),
        "std_err_eq18": fit["aux"]["std_err"],
    }


def run_smoke():
    t, X_true, W = build_benchmark()
    data = check_data(t, X_true)
    print(f"[data] t {data['t_shape']} in {data['t_range']}, "
          f"X {data['X_shape']}, finite={data['finite']}")
    assert data["finite"] and data["t_shape"][0] == cfg.M_SAMPLES
    assert data["S_starts_at_N_minus_1"] and data["I_starts_at_1"]

    r3 = r3_checks(t, X_true, W)
    ex = r3["weights_exact_vs_antiderivative"]
    conv = r3["grid_convergence"]
    print(f"[quad] weights exact to {ex['max_relative_error']:.2e}; "
          f"convergence ratios "
          f"{conv['ratio_100_to_200']:.1f}/{conv['ratio_200_to_400']:.1f} "
          f"(4th order => ~16)")
    assert ex["exact_to_machine"], ex
    assert conv["fourth_order"], conv

    nl = noiseless_check(X_true, t, W)
    print(f"[noiseless] alpha err {nl['pct_errors']['alpha']:.2e} %, "
          f"x0 max rel err {nl['x0_max_rel_err']:.2e}")
    for k, v in nl["pct_errors"].items():
        assert v < 1e-4, f"noiseless regression guard failed for {k}: {v}"

    fit = P.piwr(X_true, t, W)
    assert fit["aux"]["matrix_shape"] == [cfg.M_SAMPLES * cfg.N_STATES,
                                          cfg.N_PARAMS + cfg.N_STATES]
    assert fit["aux"]["rank"] == cfg.N_PARAMS + cfg.N_STATES
    J = P.integrate_library(P.sidr_library(X_true), W)
    assert np.max(np.abs(J[0])) == 0.0, "J_0 must be exactly zero"

    rng = np.random.default_rng(cfg.HEADLINE_SEED)
    X_noisy, _ = S.add_noise(X_true, cfg.NOISE_EPSILON, rng)
    fit_n = P.piwr(X_noisy, t, W)
    err = E.alpha_pct_error(fit_n)
    lo, hi = contract_band()
    in_band = lo <= err <= hi
    print(f"[noisy seed {cfg.HEADLINE_SEED}] alpha_hat={fit_n['alpha']:.6f}, "
          f"err={err:.4f} %, contract band [{lo:.4f}, {hi:.4f}] -> "
          f"{'in band' if in_band else 'NOT in band'}")
    print("[smoke] OK (noiseless guard + quadrature checks passed)")


def run_full():
    t_start = time.perf_counter()
    t, X_true, W = build_benchmark

def quadrature_exactness(t, X_true=None):
    """R3 implementation check: the PIWR integral library J = W @ A must equal
    a high-accuracy reference integral of the IDENTICAL not-a-knot spline.
    The reference is a dense 10-node Gauss-Legendre rule per time interval
    (exact for polynomials up to degree 21, so exact for the cubic spline up
    to rounding).  Combined abs+rel tolerance; entries whose reference value
    is near zero are skipped (relative comparison is meaningless there).
    J at j = 0 is checked to be exactly zero separately.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    if X_true is None:
        X_true = S.simulate(t)
    A = P.sidr_library(X_true)
    J = P.integrate_library(A, W := P.quadrature_weights(t))

    # dense Gauss-Legendre reference of the same spline, per library column
    x, w = np.polynomial.legendre.leggauss(10)
    dt = np.diff(t)
    ref = np.zeros_like(J)                    # (m, n, p)
    for j in range(t.size - 1):
        mid = 0.5 * (t[j] + t[j + 1])
        half = 0.5 * (t[j + 1] - t[j])
        nodes = mid + half * x
        for c in range(A.shape[1]):
            for k in range(A.shape[2]):
                sp = CubicSpline(t, A[:, c, k], bc_type=cfg.SPLINE_BC)
                val = np.sum(w * sp(nodes)) * half      # integral over [t_j, t_j+1]
                ref[j + 1:, c, k] += val

    scale = float(np.max(np.abs(ref)))
    if scale <= 0:
        return {"pass": False, "reason": "degenerate reference"}
    mask = np.abs(ref) > 1e-9 * scale
    diff = np.abs(J - ref)
    tol = 1e-9 * scale + 1e-10 * np.abs(ref)
    worst = float(np.max(diff[mask] / tol[mask]))
    return {
        "pass": bool(worst < 1.0),
        "max_abs_err": float(np.max(diff)),
        "max_rel_err_nonzero": float(np.max(diff[mask] / np.abs(ref[mask]))),
        "n_checked": int(mask.sum()),
        "n_skipped_near_zero": int(mask.size - mask.sum()),
        "gl_tol_excess": worst,
    }

def quadrature_exactness(t):
    """R3 implementation check: the weights W must integrate the not-a-knot
    cubic spline exactly, i.e. W @ f(t) == antiderivative(spline(f))(t) -
    ant(t0) to machine precision for any f (the spline is linear in its data).
    Convergence of the spline integral to the true integral is checked
    separately in quadrature_convergence.
    """
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    W = P.quadrature_weights(t)
    cases = (np.sin, np.cos, lambda s: np.exp(s / 100.0))
    worst = 0.0
    for f in cases:
        vals = f(t)
        anti = CubicSpline(t, vals, bc_type=cfg.SPLINE_BC).antiderivative()
        exact = anti(t) - anti(t[0])
        rel = float(np.max(np.abs(W @ vals - exact))) / max(
            float(np.max(np.abs(exact))), 1e-300)
        worst = max(worst, rel)
    return {"max_relative_error": worst,
            "exact_to_machine": bool(worst < 1e-12)}

def add_noise(X_true, eps, rng, variant="independent"):
    """R7 noise:  x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi.

    variant:
      "independent" - xi drawn independently per compartment and time index
                      (the reading used for the headline value).
      "shared-time" - literal R7 subscripting: ONE xi_i per time index,
                      shared by all four compartments.
    """
    X_true = np.asarray(X_true, float)
    scale = eps * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)     # per compartment
    if variant == "independent":
        xi = rng.standard_normal(X_true.shape)
    elif variant == "shared-time":
        xi = rng.standard_normal(X_true.shape[0])[:, None]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown noise variant: {variant}")
    return X_true + scale * xi, scale

def add_noise(X_true, eps, rng):
    """R7 noise: x~_c(t_i) = x_c(t_i) + eps * max_t |x_c(t)| * xi_i."""
    scale = eps * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)     # per compartment
    xi = rng.standard_normal(X_true.shape)
    return X_true + scale * xi, scale

args.new:
# ------------------------------------------------- A8 regression readings ---
#
# Non-oracle ways of damping the regressor noise (A8), all of them implementable
# inside the Section 3.2 pipeline.  In every reading the RESPONSE stays the
# noisy sample x~_j; only the library state (regressor) is pre-processed, and
# the ground-truth clean library is never a candidate (diagnostic upper bound
# only).

def smooth_moving_average(X, half_width=2):
    """Centered moving average of each compartment (window 2*h+1 samples)."""
    X = np.asarray(X, float)
    k = 2 * half_width + 1
    pad = np.pad(X, ((half_width, half_width), (0, 0)), mode="edge")
    return np.stack([
        np.convolve(pad[:, c], np.ones(k) / k, mode="valid")
        for c in range(X.shape[1])
    ], axis=1)


def smooth_reduced_knot(X, t, n_interior=9):
    """Least-squares cubic B-spline with a uniform reduced knot sequence
    (LSQUnivariateSpline), evaluated on the sample grid."""
    from scipy.interpolate import LSQUnivariateSpline
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    knots = np.linspace(t[0], t[-1], n_interior + 2)[1:-1]
    return np.stack([
        LSQUnivariateSpline(t, X[:, c], knots, k=3)(t)
        for c in range(X.shape[1])
    ], axis=1)


def smooth_smoothing_spline(X, t, sigma):
    """Cubic smoothing spline per compartment with the KNOWN design noise
    (s = m * sigma_c**2); sigma is the benchmark's noise scale, not fitted
    from ground truth."""
    from scipy.interpolate import UnivariateSpline
    t = np.asarray(t, float)
    sigma = np.asarray(sigma, float)
    return np.stack([
        UnivariateSpline(t, X[:, c], s=X.shape[0] * sigma[c] ** 2)(t)
        for c in range(X.shape[1])
    ], axis=1)


def readings_comparison(X_true, t, W, n_draws, eps, seed_base):
    """Side-by-side medians of every defensible reading of the Section 3.2
    pipeline (>= 200 draws each)."""
    out = {}
    n = n_draws
    Xs_ma = smooth_moving_average(X_true)
    Xs_rk = smooth_reduced_knot(X_true, t)
    sigma_full = eps * np.max(np.abs(X_true), axis=0)
    Xs_sp = smooth_smoothing_spline(X_true, t, sigma_full)

    def collect(make_fit, noise_variant="independent"):
        errs = np.empty(n)
        for i in range(n):
            rng = np.random.default_rng(seed_base + i)
            Xn, _ = S.add_noise(X_true, eps, rng, variant=noise_variant)
            errs[i] = alpha_pct_error(make_fit(Xn, rng))
        return summarize(errs)

    # 1. locked: library evaluated at the noisy samples (paper p. 17 / 5.10)
    out["locked_noisy_library"] = collect(lambda Xn, r: P.piwr(Xn, t, W))
    # 2. literal R7 subscripting: one xi per time index, shared by all states
    out["shared_time_literal_R7"] = collect(
        lambda Xn, r: P.piwr(Xn, t, W), noise_variant="shared-time")
    # 3. scalar noise scale from the infected compartment's max
    out["scalar_sigma_from_I"] = collect(
        lambda Xn, r: P.piwr(Xn, t, W), noise_variant="scalar_from_I")
    # 4. library evaluated on a moving-average smoothed state
    def f_ma(Xn, r):
        Xs = smooth_moving_average(Xn)
        return P.piwr(Xn, t, W, library="explicit", X_library=Xs)
    out["smoothed_moving_average_library"] = collect(f_ma)
    # 5. library evaluated on a reduced-knot B-spline smoothed state
    def f_rk(Xn, r):
        Xs = smooth_reduced_knot(Xn, t)
        return P.piwr(Xn, t, W, library="explicit", X_library=Xs)
    out["smoothed_reduced_knot_library"] = collect(f_rk)
    # 6. library evaluated on a smoothing-spline state (known design sigma)
    def f_sp(Xn, r):
        Xs = smooth_smoothing_spline(Xn, t, sigma_full)
        return P.piwr(Xn, t, W, library="explicit", X_library=Xs)
    out["smoothed_smoothing_spline_library"] = collect(f_sp)
    # 7. compartment-max row scaling (statistically it is 1/sigma_c weighting)
    out["row_scaled_compartment_max"] = collect(
        lambda Xn, r: P.piwr(Xn, t, W, row_scaling="compartment-max"))
    # 8. clean-library control: diagnostic UPPER BOUND, never the headline
    out["clean_library_control_upper_bound"] = collect(
        lambda Xn, r: P.piwr(Xn, t, W, library="clean", X_library=X_true))
    return out

args.summary:
Reimplemented the paper's PIWR (physics-informed weak regression) for the COVID-19 SIDR benchmark from the text (arXiv:2610.19058) — no code for the paper's method exists in the linked DINN repo (it is the baseline, notebooks only). `python reproduce.py` runs end-to-end in ~20-28 s, exits 0, and writes results/metrics.json.

WHAT WAS BUILT (per requirements R1-R7, R12-R15): SIDR vector field per the paper's eqs. (5)/(28) (dD=γI, dR=βI — verified identical to the DINN generator notebook and tutorial), LSODA at 1e-10 (R15); not-a-knot cubic-spline quadrature weights W built once per grid, library integrated exactly (R3, verified to 2e-15 relative against a dense Gauss-Legendre reference of the identical spline, plus 4th-order grid convergence 20.6/17.3); weak-form system x_j = x0 + J_j θ with joint x0 (R2, R4); unit-column-norm scaling and numpy.linalg.lstsq (SVD), never normal equations (R5, R6); compartment-max row scaling as the paper's tuned option, selected by the paper's own 200-draw tuning protocol (5.9); R7 noise ε·max_t|x_c| independent per compartment/time; errors as % of the true value (R14). Data generator validated against all three DINN CSVs (sidr.csv, Experiments/noise/sidr_100_pts.csv, COVID_Tutorial.csv) to 3.4e-8 max relative diff.

RESULTS (all computed, none typed): C1 headline (fixed seed 0, declared a priori): α̂=0.188941, error 1.0780 % — OUTSIDE the ±10 % band around the reported 0.124 % (band [0.1116, 0.1364]), on the high side. 1000-draw distribution: median 0.7301 %, mean 0.842 %, IQR [0.3529, 1.2120] %, 5-95 % [0.0646, 2.1131] %, min 0.0036 %, max 3.534 %; the paper's 0.124 % sits at the 9.7th percentile, i.e. consistent with a favorable unstated draw but not with the center of the distribution. C2 noise-free: α error 3.79e-5 % (reported 1.05e-4 %, same order), x0 recovered to 2.3e-7. C5 timing: median 0.495 ms per fit over 30 repeats (reported 0.21 ms, same order, different hardware).

HONEST DEPARTURE, DOCUMENTED NOT TUNED: the 1 %-noise α median (0.73 %) is ~5.9× the reported 0.124 %. Diagnostics pin the cause: (i) error grows exactly LINEARLY in ε (0.064/0.161/0.324/0.652 % at ε=0.001/0.0025/0.005/0.01) with near-zero mean bias → first-order variance inflation, not attenuation; (ii) eq.(18) σ_α = 0.140 % vs observed spread 0.966 % (ratio 6.9) → the linear covariance model does not track the noisy-regressor error; (iii) block breakdown shows the α-regressor integral carries most of it (S-only 0.686 %, I-only 1.307 %); (iv) the clean-library control (oracle, upper bound only) gives median 0.129 % — right at the paper's 0.124 % — isolating the gap to the library-evaluated-at-noisy-samples term, which the paper itself flags in §5.10 ("Both PIR and PIWR evaluate the library at the noisy samples"). A8 readings side by side (200 draws each): locked 0.652 %, literal shared-time R7 0.822 %, scalar-σ-from-I 0.555 %, moving-average-smoothed library 1.794 %, reduced-knot 6.935 %, smoothing-spline 0.755 %, compartment-max row scaling 0.645 % — no non-oracle reading reaches the reported value; smoothing the regressor biases it. β/γ medians under noise (0.455 %/0.495 %) DO match the paper's Table 2 β/γ (0.487 %/0.46 %).

The requested DINN multiplicative-noise (σ_ci = ε·|x_c(t_i)|) 1000-draw diagnostic was NOT run — the stop instruction arrived first; it is the one outstanding cheap check.

The one-off inspection one-liners' key-name mismatches were fixed in the final validation (JSON keys verified: metric/value/headline.alpha_pct_error/sweep_1000_draws/a8_readings_comparison). Assumptions A19-A21 recorded in the ledger. reproduce.py --smoke (fast gates: R3 quadrature, noiseless recovery, matrix rank/shape, noisy-fit sanity) also exits 0.

target.statement: PIWR estimates the COVID-19 SIDR transmission rate α with 0.124 % relative error at 1 % measurement noise.
target.table_ref: Table 2, row α, column PIWR / PIWR-RACC under noise level ε = 0.01

tolerance.why: Rule 4: the target is a relative % error with no reported std for this row and is an unbounded error metric, so use a 10 % relative band around 0.124 %, i.e. about 0.1116–0.1364 % error.

audit_summary: The PIWR point-estimate implementation is faithful for C1: parameter-linear library, not-a-knot cubic-spline quadrature, joint x0, SVD least squares with unit-column scaling, LSODA 1e-10, and the SIDR grid/parameters cross-check against DINN to 3.4e-8. The clean rerun computes α error 1.078% for seed 0 and a 1000-draw median 0.730% (IQR 0.353–1.212%), so the paper's 0.124% is outside the 10% band and sits at the 9.7th percentile of the run's realizations; this is a failed numeric match, not a different dataset/metric/method. The main fidelity caveat is R7: the headline uses independent per-compartment/time ξ, while the literal quoted ξ_i is shared across compartments; both variants were run and both miss the target. Conformal requirements R8–R11 are absent because C1 is only a point estimate, but they would be missing for the full conformalized method. No computed result is hard-coded or echoed from the paper—the 0.124 constant is used only for comparison—and the run is full-scale; the divergence is best attributed to the paper's unstated noise realization/randomness (A1/A20/A21), with a documented A20-vs-code inconsistency (A20 says median draw, code uses seed 0).

requirement_check.evidence: src/piwr.py sidr_library builds A(x,t) for S,I,D,R with observed states and known N only; θ=(α,β,γ) are the physical parameters, so A contains no unknowns.
fit_with assembles M=[J,I_n] and y=X~, i.e. x_j=x0+J_jθ with J=integrate_library(A,W); no data differentiation is used.
quadrature_weights integrates not-a-knot CubicSpline unit basis functions exactly; smoke checks report max relative quadrature error 2e-15 and fourth-order convergence ratios 20.6/17.3.
x0 is part of z=(θ,x0) in fit_with, with identity entries M[r,p+c]=1 for the corresponding state row.
The point solve uses numpy.linalg.lstsq(Ms,y) (SVD-based); normal equations are not formed for the solve. pinv(Ms.T@Ms) is used only for covariance diagnostics, not for the estimate.
fit_with computes column norms, scales live columns to unit norm, solves, then unscales z; column scaling is a change of variables.

add_noise uses the correct per-compartment scale ε·max_t|x_c(t)|, but the headline default draws independent ξ per compartment and time; the literal shared-time ξ_i variant is also implemented and gives 1000-draw median 0.798% vs independent 0.730%. Both are disclosed, and neither reaches 0.124%.
No conformal prior-box calibration code is implemented; C1 is only a point-estimate target, but the full paper requirement is absent.
No maximum-normalized-error split-conformal nonconformity score or simultaneous quantile is implemented.
No PIWR-RACC residual-adaptive factor h=1+R/Rbar or 200-draw Rbar tuning is implemented.
No 999-calibration-problem, α=0.1 conformal pipeline is implemented.
For SIDR the parameter map h is identity (θ=(α,β,γ)); fit_with returns α,β,γ and eq.(18) standard errors from the covariance, which is the identity-map delta-method result.
config.py sets N=59e6, x0=(N−1,1,0,0), α=0.191, β=0.05, γ=0.0294, and np.linspace(0,500,100); the generated SIDR trajectory matches DINN CSVs to 3.4e-8 max relative difference.

evaluate.pct_error implements 100·|estimate−actual|/|actual|; C1 uses the α error, where the median over one estimated parameter is the parameter itself. No model-level median summary was needed for C1.
